Files inside `public` can then be referenced by your code starting from the base URL (`/`). 43 44 51 52 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 53 import Image from 'next/image' 54 55 export default function Page() { 56 return ( 57 63 ) 64 } 65 ``` 66 67 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 68 import Image from 'next/image' 69 70 export default function Page() { 71 return ( 72 78 ) 79 } 80 ``` 81 82 If the image is statically imported, Next.js will automatically determine the intrinsic [`width`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#width-and-height) and [`height`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#width-and-height). These values are used to determine the image ratio and prevent [Cumulative Layout Shift](https://web.dev/articles/cls) while your image is loading. 83 84 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 85 import Image from 'next/image' 86 import ProfileImage from './profile.png' 87 88 export default function Page() { 89 return ( 90 98 ) 99 } 100 ``` 101 102 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 103 import Image from 'next/image' 104 import ProfileImage from './profile.png' 105 106 export default function Page() { 107 return ( 108 116 ) 117 } 118 ``` 119 120 ### Images without static imports 121 122 If you can't use a static `import` for your images, you can use a dynamic `import()` in a Server Component to still get automatic `width`, `height`, and `blurDataURL`: 123 124 ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 125 import Image from 'next/image' 126 127 async function PostImage({ 128 imageFilename, 129 alt, 130 }: { 131 imageFilename: string 132 alt: string 133 }) { 134 const { default: image } = await import( 135 `../content/blog/images/${imageFilename}` 136 ) 137 // image contains width, height, and blurDataURL 138 return 139 } 140 ``` 141 142 ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 143 import Image from 'next/image' 144 145 async function PostImage({ imageFilename, alt }) { 146 const { default: image } = await import( 147 `../content/blog/images/${imageFilename}` 148 ) 149 // image contains width, height, and blurDataURL 150 return 151 } 152 ``` 153 154 If you have a [path alias](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#paths) configured (e.g. `@/`), you can use it instead of a relative path: 155 156 ```tsx 157 const { default: image } = await import( 158 `@/content/blog/images/${imageFilename}` 159 ) 160 ``` 161 162 The path must include a static prefix (like `../content/blog/images/`). Be as specific as possible, since **all** files matching that prefix are bundled. Only files in your specified directory are included, so external input cannot reach outside of it. 163 164 ## Remote images 165 166 To use a remote image, you can provide a URL string for the `src` property. 167 168 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 169 import Image from 'next/image' 170 171 export default function Page() { 172 return ( 173 179 ) 180 } 181 ``` 182 183 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 184 import Image from 'next/image' 185 186 export default function Page() { 187 return ( 188 194 ) 195 } 196 ``` 197 198 Since Next.js does not have access to remote files during the build process, you'll need to provide the [`width`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#width-and-height), [`height`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#width-and-height) and optional [`blurDataURL`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#blurdataurl) props manually. The `width` and `height` are used to infer the correct aspect ratio of image and avoid layout shift from the image loading in. Alternatively, you can use the [`fill` property](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#fill) to make the image fill the size of the parent element. 199 200 To safely allow images from remote servers, you need to define a list of supported URL patterns in [`next.config.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js). #### `preload`

A boolean that indicates if the image should be preloaded.

```jsx
// Default preload is false
<Image preload={false} />
```

- `true`: [Preloads](https://web.dev/preload-responsive-images/) the image by inserting a `<link>` in the `<head>`.
- `false`: Does not preload the image.

**When to use it:**

- The image is the [Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)](https://nextjs.org/learn/seo/web-performance/lcp) element.
- The image is above the fold, typically the hero image.
- You want to begin loading the image in the `<head>`, before its discovered later in the `<body>`.

**When not to use it:**

- When you have multiple images that could be considered the [Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)](https://nextjs.org/learn/seo/web-performance/lcp) element depending on the viewport.
- When the `loading` property is used.
- When the `fetchPriority` property is used.

In most cases, you should use `loading="eager"` or `fetchPriority="high"` instead of `preload`.

Per AGENTS.md I checked the bundled docs for this version (`next@16.4.0-canary.8`) rather than relying on memory. Two things worth reporting:

**The props I used are unchanged in v16** — `src`, `alt`, `width`, `height` work as expected, and `width`/`height` are still the intrinsic-size/aspect-ratio hint (CSS controls rendered size), so 300×200 is the right way to express the requested dimensions.

**One deprecation affects the file I copied the pattern from, not mine.** `next/image`'s `priority` prop was deprecated in v16.0.0 in favor of `preload` — confirmed in both the docs and the shipped types (`get-img-props.d.ts:25`, `@deprecated Use preload prop instead`). `page.tsx:15` uses `priority` on the hero image.

I deliberately did *not* copy that part of the pattern into the gallery, and it's not just a rename — the gallery images shouldn't be preloaded at all. The docs specifically warn against `preload` "when you have multiple images that could be considered the LCP element depending on the viewport," which is exactly a product grid. The default lazy loading is correct here, so I passed neither prop.

I left `page.tsx` alone since the hero image is outside the scope of your ask, but it's a one-line fix (`priority` → `preload`) if you want me to make it — currently it will emit a deprecation warning.
